sources.title: Jacques Le Goff, interview by Silvia Pérez Ringuelet (Paris, December 1988), published 1991.
sources.citation: Silvia Pérez Ringuelet, “Entrevista al profesor Jacques Le Goff,” Boletín de Historia Social Europea 3 (1991), pp.57–68; interview in Paris, December 1988.

verification.note: Fresh primary Spanish interview text read on printed pp.57–63, with pp.59–61 also visually checked. Le Goff’s answers are separated from the interviewer’s questions and reported quotations. Interview 1988 and publication 1991 remain distinct. The account qualifies its criticism of Braudel and praises Duby’s Bouvines; neither underlying work was newly read. Later interview pages64–68 were not read as evidence for these proposals.

sources.title: Jacques Le Goff, acknowledgments and preface to the new edition of La Nouvelle Histoire (1988).
sources.citation: Jacques Le Goff, “Préface à la nouvelle édition (1988),” La Nouvelle Histoire (Brussels: Éditions Complexe, 1988), opening p.9 and unnumbered acknowledgments; original collective encyclopedia 1978.

verification.note: Fresh selected primary transcription of copyright/frontmatter, acknowledgments and opening 1988 preface p.9 read. The text explicitly credits Roger Chartier and Jacques Revel; collaboration concerns the 1978 project. Bibliographic 1978 editorial credits independently corroborated in the Grenoble library record https://bm-grenoble.fr/detailstatic.aspx?RSC_BASE=SYRACUSE&RSC_DOCID=831465&TITLE=la-nouvelle-histoire-sous-la-dir-de-jacques-le-goff&_lg=fr-FR . This is primary text displayed by a third-party host, not a publisher-hosted facsimile or whole-book reading. The site’s AI summary is not evidence; no intellectual influence is inferred from editorial credit.

hc171_legoff_ephe.note: Institutional notice read, including Schmitt-attributed paragraph on the 1964 synthesis and bibliographic list. Argument claims remain mediated by this named reader; Le Goff’s book itself unread. Notice records birth 1924 and death 1 April 2014. Les Intellectuels is dated 1957 in the narrative but 1956 in its list; neither is adopted as a new event. Additional fresh reading, 2026-10-25: the opening Schmitt-attributed paragraph under “Domaines de recherches” explicitly associates the change from historical sociology to medieval historical anthropology with the growing influence of Lévi-Strauss and others. This is Schmitt’s account, not Le Goff’s own testimony, and establishes neither personal mentorship nor exclusive methodological allegiance. The same page’s 1974 joint-editing credit was checked only as research context.
